refs: Method: no channel split is published for this country, so each channel share is a benchmark estimate anchored on the published German (BRV 2024: 71 / 20 / 3 / 6%) and French splits and adjusted for the country context noted below. Treat the shares as placeholders with an error of roughly +/-6 points until your team replaces them.

UK: independent garages dominate and fast-fit networks are stable or growing, while franchised dealers have been losing share (Mintel, qualitative; the numbers are paywalled). Online is a growing but smaller channel.
Market size: Estimate: 36.2M licensed cars (DfT, end-2024) x about 0.80 tyres per car per year. An older GfK/NTDA study put the market at 28.4M

BTMA/EuroPool: members sold 9.330M UK consumer replacement tyres (passenger car, SUV, light commercial) in H1 2024, as reported by European Rubber Journal. Doubled to 18.7M for the year; seasonality and stock timing are why the range is 18.2-19.3M. The research also quotes 4.786M for Q2 2024 (not checked).

Pool versus market: 29.0M less 18.7M leaves about 10.3M (35%) outside the EuroPool members. BTMA links member volumes to low-cost imports, particularly from China and Vietnam (European Rubber Journal). The research also quotes extra-EU passenger and light-truck imports up 10% in 2024 and well above 30M tyres a year, and GfK's 2023 UK mix of 33% premium, 22% mid-range and 45% budget. None of that was checked here, and customs imports cannot go in the import box because they include pool brands, OE supply and stock.

Wholesale structure: Micheldever supplies about 6.0M tyres a year (Sumitomo Rubber Industries agreed to buy it in January 2017). Stapleton's calls itself the UK's largest distributor, with 11 locations, and has been owned by Itochu since 1994. The research also cites more than 7,000 independent customers for Stapleton's and more than 6,000 retailers for Micheldever (not checked). Do not add these up: they include own retail and overlapping customers.

Halfords sold its Viking distribution business to Bond International in FY2024, expecting savings of about 5M GBP a year while keeping the margin benefits of direct sourcing (Tyrepress). It shows why direct versus wholesale is blurry: sourcing can be direct while stock and delivery run through a distributor.

Wholesale versus direct is an inference from market structure, about 72 / 28 with a range of 67-78% wholesale, not a reported percentage. Channel routing has the lowest confidence of all: specialists about 82% via wholesale, dealers 54%, other retail 75%, online 39%.

Ownership (research, not checked): Micheldever and Protyre belong to Sumitomo Rubber, Stapleton's and Kwik Fit sit within Itochu's European Tyre Enterprise, and Blackcircles is Michelin-owned. The large UK wholesalers are therefore not independent in the ownership sense.

Private versus commercial is a mileage proxy. The research quotes DfT 2024 Great Britain vehicle miles of 256.1bn for cars and taxis and 58.5bn for vans, which puts vans at about 18.6% of the total and about 5.4M of the 29.0M tyres. Not checked here.

market.source: Research estimate for passenger-car tyres only, not a VACO figure (VACO publishes no unit total). RecyBEM collected 10.53M tyres in 2024 and its final 2024 balance of -538,000 implies about 9.99M placed (both as quoted by the research). That scope also covers light-truck and trailer/caravan tyres, so the research takes 79-82% of it (7.9-8.2M). Working range 7.7-8.4M. Replaces the earlier 7.2M.

industry.source: Research model, low confidence: the part of the 8.0M supplied by the major-brand (industry pool) manufacturers. Not a published ETRMA or Tyres Europe country figure.

toWs.source: Research model: of the 6.5M industry volume, 3.75M goes through wholesale and 2.75M direct to the channels. Central case 66% wholesale overall (range 58-72%), not a published percentage.

export.source: Model convention only. Customs data (UN Comtrade, as quoted by the research) show 21.16M passenger-car tyres exported and 31.75M imported in 2024, but those flows include re-export and transit trade and cannot be used in a domestic balance. It does not mean the Netherlands exported nothing.

Market size: RecyBEM's 2025 balance reports about 9.9M tyres placed and 10.4M collected, in a scope that includes light-truck and trailer/caravan tyres (up to 3.5 t). For 2024 it reports 10.53M collected, and with the final negative balance of 538,000 that implies about 9.99M placed. I could not confirm these RecyBEM figures on the pages I could open. The research takes 79-82% as passenger cars, giving 8.0M for 2024 and about 7.9M for 2025 (range 7.6-8.3M), broadly flat.

Parc and mileage (confirmed on CBS): Dutch passenger cars drove about 122 billion km in 2024, privately owned cars about 11,100 km and company cars about 20,300 km each, and the parc passed 9.4M cars on 1 January 2026 (+1.8%). The research quotes 87.7% of cars as privately owned. Weighting by mileage gives about 80% private and 20% commercial tyre demand.

Customs versus domestic balance: UN Comtrade (as quoted by the research, not checked) shows 31.746M passenger-car tyres (HS 401110) imported and 21.160M exported in 2024. Net imports of 10.59M already exceed the whole Dutch market, so gross customs figures describe a distribution and re-export hub and are not used in the domestic balance.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split, not a published figure: 3.75M of the 6.5M industry volume goes through wholesale, 2.75M goes direct, and the 1.5M of non-pool supply is routed through wholesalers and importers. That gives 5.25M wholesale and 2.75M direct (66 / 34, range 58-72% wholesale).

Wholesale layer: Inter-Sprint's own site says it supplies tyre specialists, wholesalers and parts distributors. The research quotes about 2.7M tyres in stock and more than 17,000 SKUs; a 2022 trade article reported about 2.8M and 16,000, so the scale matches, but I could not confirm the current figures. Heuver's own site presents it as a B2B wholesaler for truck, agricultural and earthmoving tyres and does not mention passenger-car tyres, so it is no longer shown as a passenger-car wholesaler. Van den Ban stays as a major passenger-car gateway (not confirmed on its website).

Latest signals: BOVAG's August 2025 sample found almost 39% of cars on all-season tyres. That is a fleet fitment share, not a replacement sales mix. RecyBEM notes that private purchases from foreign online sellers can fall outside the Dutch placement statistics, so the online box is partly invisible in official data.

refs: Method (replaced with the Italy research file): the channel volumes follow the research's model of 72.9 / 15.7 / 2.6 / 8.8%, replacing the earlier benchmark of 68 / 12 / 3 / 17% on a 33M market. Only the specialist total has a measured anchor; the other three channels and every route split are modelled allocations.

Specialist anchor: NIQ-GfK, as quoted by the research in March 2026, put specialised tyre-dealer sales at 19.6M in 2025, down 0.4%, which implies 19.68M in 2024. I could not find that release. What I could confirm is the older GfK series for the same panel: 19.7M tyres in 2022, also down 0.4% (GfK, September 2023), covering passenger-car, light-truck and 4x4/SUV tyres. So the order of magnitude holds, but the scope may include light trucks.

Market size: 19.68M divided by a 72.9% specialist share gives 27.0M. The 69-77% sensitivity gives 25.6-28.5M. The research cross-checks it at about 0.65 tyres per car on a parc of about 41.3M cars (ACI/ACEA, as quoted, not checked) and expects 2025 to be flat at 26.8-27.0M. The earlier 33M converted MASE's 421,645 tonnes, which cover all tyre types.

Customs versus domestic balance: UN Comtrade (as quoted by the research, not checked) shows 35.735M HS 401110 passenger-car tyres imported (9.04M from China) and 18.467M exported in 2024. Net imports of 17.3M reflect Italy's role as a manufacturing and distribution hub, so customs data are not used in the import or export boxes.

Non-pool supply: the research quotes NIQ-GfK's extrapool share at 14.7% of specialist volume in 2025, up 26% in a year, which implies about 11.7% (about 2.30M tyres) in 2024. Adding online and other retail gives about 3.4M non-pool tyres consumed in Italy, plus 0.7M re-exported, so 4.1M. On 7 July 2026 the European Commission imposed definitive anti-dumping duties of 4.3% to 45.3% on Chinese passenger-car and light-truck tyres (confirmed, Eunews). China supplied almost 93M such tyres to the EU in 2024, a 28% share.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split: 13.2M of the 23.6M industry volume goes through wholesale and 10.4M direct, plus 4.1M non-pool imports, less 0.7M re-exported, gives 16.6M wholesale sold in Italy (about 61.5%) and 10.4M direct (about 38.5%). The 13.2M is a residual that reconciles the model, not an observed figure.

Wholesalers (checked): Fintyre's own site states over 6M tyres a year, 2 hubs, 10-12 warehouses and more than 50 brands, through three companies: Fintyre, Franco Gomme and Gexpo Tyre. Tyrepress reported Univergomma's 2023 revenue above 335M EUR (up 5%, car segment growing). Atoka lists Zuin as a tyre and auto-parts wholesaler in San Pietro in Gu with latest declared revenue of 89.4M EUR. Tyre Trends (May 2024) describes Magri Group as a national multi-brand distributor of car, truck and agricultural tyres working with the CDG and Kwik Fit networks.

Wholesale volumes are the research's PCR estimates, converted from all-category disclosures, not company figures: Fintyre about 4.5M (4.0-5.0M), Univergomma 3.1M (2.6-3.6M), Magri 1.5M (0.9-2.0M), Zuin 1.0M (0.8-1.3M), Pneus In 0.6M, Palmeri 0.45M, Intergomma 0.35M, regional importers about 1.2M combined. Not confirmed: Univergomma's 5M pieces in 2024 and 1M tyres in stock, Zuin's 86M EUR for 2024 and 500+ points of sale, Magri's 60% car share of revenue, and the Pneus In, Palmeri, Intergomma, Pneutec, Piùgomme and PR Sud details. Tagliabue Gomme Gross and Carlini Gomme, already on the list, are not covered by the research.

Latest signals (research, not checked): all-season tyres reached 31.6% of specialist volume in 2025, up from 21.8% in 2020, with all-season volume up 3.0%, summer down 1.8% and winter down 2.0%. Michelin's market indicator shows European replacement demand broadly stable through August 2026. Older carried-over note: trade claims of very high online volumes come from sponsored articles and were not used.

refs: Method (replaced with the Austria research file): every figure is a model estimate for passenger-car tyres only. The channel shares of 72 / 18 / 3 / 7% are kept from the earlier benchmark and rescaled from 4.6M (car, van and 4x4) to 4.5M. No public Austrian source gives a sell-out total or a channel split.

Market size: the research found no complete 2024 or 2025 Austrian sell-out figure. The GfK retail panel supported by VRO recorded almost 3.6M tyres in 2018 and is not all-channel coverage (I could not open that source). Working range 4.3-4.7M. The parc supports it: the research quotes 5.23M passenger cars at the end of 2024 (Statistics Austria), and ORF reports 5.29M at the end of 2025, up 54,208.

Customs versus domestic balance: UN Comtrade (as quoted by the research, not checked) shows 9.056M HS 401110 passenger-car tyres imported and 1.296M exported in 2024. Net imports of 7.76M exceed the estimated sell-out because customs data include original-equipment supply, distributor stock and re-export, so they are not used in the import or export boxes.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split, not a published figure: 0.75M of the 3.6M industry volume goes through wholesale and 2.85M goes direct, plus 1.70M of non-pool supply, less 0.80M re-exported, gives 1.65M wholesale sold in Austria (about 37%) and 2.85M direct (about 63%). Direct is broader than factory-to-shop. BestDrive is Continental-owned and Euromaster is Michelin-owned, so a large part of retail is supplied outside independent wholesale.

Wholesalers (checked): AUTO PLUS Reifen is a subsidiary of Wolfgang Denzel Auto AG and is described by the Denzel Group as one of Austria's leading tyre importers and wholesalers with more than 2,000 dealer partners (Denzel press release, September 2022; Reifenpresse, January 2023). Tire Network's own site calls it a wholesaler for tyres, rims and complete wheels in Austria with over 50,000 tyres in stock, ordered through a members-only B2B shop for dealers and fitting partners; it is registered in Vienna (founded 2022). ARG Reifengrosshandel GmbH is registered in Dornbirn (WKO).

Wholesale volumes are the research's estimates, not company figures: Auto Plus about 0.6M PCR tyres a year (range 0.45-0.8M), Tire Network about 0.15M (0.10-0.20M), ARG about 0.05M domestic (0.03-0.08M), Delticom's Autoreifenonline.at B2B about 0.10M. I could not confirm Auto Plus's 350,000-tyre pre-season stock or 1,500 peak orders a day, or ARG's roughly 50% export quota. Delticom is treated as cross-border supply, not as an Austrian wholesaler.

Retail network corrections (checked): Forstinger now states 69 branches and 68 specialist workshops (earlier page: about 111). Lucky Car took over 24 former A.T.U sites in February 2024 (more than 270 jobs) and had 44 locations before, around 70 afterwards per LEADERSNET (the research says 60+). A 2022 Continental release announced that Profi Reifen and Reifen John would be renamed BestDrive over about two years, with over 50 workshops. Point S: the research quotes over 60 service locations from its site, while a 2022 UTA release quoted 100.

Latest signals (research, not checked): Tyres Europe reports European consumer replacement tyres up 2% in H1 2026, with all-season up 9%, summer down 2% and winter down 5%. Austria's situational winter-equipment rule runs from 1 November to 15 April. The research expects a 2026 run-rate of 4.5-4.6M but does not treat it as a published figure.

The import box is the research's 1.10M estimate of non-pool imports feeding Hungarian wholesalers, and the export box its 0.25M estimate of distributor re-export. meta.scopeNote: The card header's 3.1M is HTA's 2018 total for all tyre categories, including light-commercial tyres. This model's 2.85M is a 2024 estimate for passenger cars plus SUV/4x4 only. The research does not cover private versus commercial demand, so those boxes still need input.

refs: Method (replaced with the Hungary research file): the market and every flow and channel figure are modelled for passenger-car plus SUV/4x4 tyres, excluding light commercial. The channel shares of 70 / 10 / 5 / 15% are kept from the earlier benchmark and rescaled from 2.8M to 2.85M. No Hungarian source publishes sell-out by channel.

HTA 2018 (confirmed): the Hungarian Tyre Association reported 3.1M tyres sold in 2018 (up 9.7%) through manufacturers' representatives, of which passenger-car 2.4M (up 9%), SUV 182,000 (up 23%) and light commercial 258,000 (up 5%) (444.hu, January 2019). That gives about 2.6M for passenger cars plus SUVs. The older 3.1M card header is the all-category total.

2024 estimate: KSH reports 4.37M passenger cars at the end of 2025, up 111,000 (2.6%) in the year, so about 4.26M at the end of 2024, with an average age of about 16.5 years (confirmed). The research quotes 3.642M cars at the end of 2018, so the parc is about 17% larger. Applying 2018's 0.714 tyres per car would give about 3.05M; the research uses 2.85M (range 2.65-3.05M) because replacement demand has been weak since the post-Covid price shock, citing an Apollo executive's roughly 30% decline comment (not checked). Its 2025 figure (about 2.80M) and 2026 run-rate (about 2.90M) are estimates; the Tyres Europe changes it quotes (down 2% in 2025, up 2% in H1 2026) are European, not Hungarian, and not checked.

Customs versus domestic balance: customs data are not used. Hungary is a major tyre production and export hub (the research quotes HTA: 34.1M tyres produced in 2022), so import and export statistics include original-equipment supply, factory output and re-export. The 1.10M import and 0.25M export boxes are the research's estimates of non-pool distributor flows.

Wholesale versus direct is a modelled split of about 74 / 26, not a published figure: 1.25M of the 2.00M industry volume goes through wholesale and 0.75M goes direct, plus 1.10M of non-pool imports, less 0.25M re-exported, gives 2.10M wholesale sold in Hungary (74%) and 0.75M direct (26%).

Wholesalers (checked): AKH is a Hungarian family-owned company that says it sells more than one million tyres a year and had more than 200 reseller partners in its service programme (Vilaggazdasag 2021 and 2022). MARSO is a tyre wholesaler with more than 1,000 resellers and 30 stores in 2020, and 2019 revenue of HUF 27.3bn (Vilaggazdasag). Not confirmed: AKH's claims of 2,000 reseller partners and being the largest player, MARSO's 16 regional warehouses, the 2024 domestic sales of HUF 33.0bn (MARSO) and HUF 27.1bn (AKH), and Bridgestone's 2023 move of distribution to MARSO.

Caution on wholesaler volumes: the research estimates 0.65-0.80M PCR for AKH and 0.55-0.70M for MARSO. In 2022 AKH's deputy CEO put its market share at around 10% (Economx), which is hard to reconcile with 23-28% of 2.85M, so treat these volumes as upper-end estimates. The earlier note that MARSO holds exclusive Michelin and Bridgestone agreements is removed because I found no support for it.

Manufacturer layer: the research names Apollo, Bridgestone, Continental, Goodyear, Hankook, Michelin and Pirelli as having Hungarian sales entities (HTA, as quoted, not checked). They supply distributors and large accounts directly and sit behind the industry and direct boxes. The Gumi.hu network size differs: this page says 150+ service points, the research 100+ workshop stations. Left as is.
